newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Salomon rates Russia's Bashkirenergo a 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: Salomon rates Russia's Bashkirenergo a 'buy'.

text.p: Shares in Russian regional utility Bashkirenergo represent good value despite recent price strength, Salomon Brothers said.

"Although the shares have performed quite well over the past month (up 63 percent relative to the ASP General index), we see significant near-term as well as long-term upside remaining," it said in a research note by analyst Alexander Kazbegi dated February 18.

It recommended buying shares in Bashkirenergo, Russia's seventh largest utility, because it owns all its operating assets. The company is largely independent from national power company RAO UES, which has only a 21 percent stake.
UES owns large stakes in all but a handful of Russia's regional "energo" power companies.
Bashkirenergo is currently listed on the Russian Trading System's RTS-2 second-tier market for less liquid stocks.

It has a stable customer base of oil and gas companies in the autonomous republic of Bashkortostan, it said. The company also has an appealing valuation with low multiples relative to comparable Russian and international companies, it said.
The company's progressive management also makes it an attractive buy, the report said. "Management is expected to take progressive measures to improve transparency and openness," it said.

Preferred shares offer a good prospective U.S. dollar dividend yield of 10 percent in 1997 and are clearly the best avenue of investment in the company, it said. Investment risks are the low liquidity of the stock and potential share dilution from a possible swap of the state's debt for equity, it said.
